name: Kinesiology / face taping
summary: Elastic sports tape applied to the face to 'retrain' muscles; the tape's general evidence is weak and facial use is untested.
lead: Kinesiology or face taping is the application of elastic therapeutic tape, of the kind developed for sports and musculoskeletal use, to the face. In appearance-focused communities it is described as a way to retrain facial muscles, lift or hold tissue, or reduce puffiness.

name: Facial nerve rehab / neurectomy
summary: Medical and surgical care for asymmetry caused by facial nerve paralysis; an established clinical field, not a cosmetic add-on for normal faces.
lead: Facial nerve rehabilitation and neurectomy refer to medical and surgical approaches for facial asymmetry caused by facial nerve paralysis. Rehabilitation involves therapy and exercise techniques, and surgical options include nerve repair, grafting, nerve transfers and muscle transfers. Neurectomy means cutting or removing part of a nerve.

name: Tongue tie release
summary: Frenotomy releases the tissue under the tongue; it has feeding evidence in infants, but claims about facial symmetry are untested.
lead: Tongue-tie release, also called frenotomy or frenectomy, is a minor surgical procedure that cuts or removes the lingual frenulum, the fold of tissue anchoring the tongue to the floor of the mouth, in people with ankyloglossia (tongue-tie). It can be done with scissors, a scalpel or a laser, and a related procedure, frenuloplasty, adds suturing for more complex cases.

name: Camera angle / eye dominance selection
summary: Picking a 'better side' for photos; faces are measurably asymmetric, but no source links eye dominance to a flattering angle.
lead: Camera angle and eye dominance selection is the practice of choosing which side of the face, and which angle, to present to a camera, sometimes with reference to a person's dominant eye. The idea is that most faces look better from one side than the other.

name: Dental midline correction
summary: Aligning the centre line of the teeth; the concept is defined, but sources reviewed give no evidence on its appearance effect.
lead: Dental midline correction is the adjustment of teeth, usually through orthodontic treatment, so that the midline between the upper or lower central incisors lines up with the midline of the face or the opposing arch. The dental midline is defined as the midsagittal line of the upper and lower dental arches when the teeth are in maximum intercuspation and have ideal size, shape and position.

name: Lighting / smiling side meta
summary: Picking your good side, lighting it well and evening out your smile; popular as a photo tactic, with no direct research behind it.
lead: The lighting and smiling side meta is a set of photo-and-presentation tactics in looksmaxxing circles concerned with which side of the face is shown to a camera, how the light falls on it, and how evenly a person smiles. The stated aim is to make a face look more symmetrical or more attractive in photographs and in person by working around uneven smiles and lopsided features.

name: Neck training (flexion/extension)
summary: Forward/back neck exercises for a thicker neck; well studied for pain and sport, not for looks.
lead: Neck training in the flexion and extension sense means exercising the neck forward and backward against resistance, often with a towel, hands, plate or machine. In looksmaxxing forums it is promoted as a way to build a thicker, stronger neck that proponents say complements the jaw, physique and posture.
claims: A thicker neck improves overall looks and physique
Training one side more can make the neck asymmetrical
Neck training can cause sleep apnea

name: Neck bridges / wrestler bridges
summary: A wrestling-style arch on the head and feet used to thicken the neck; no appearance research exists.
lead: A neck bridge, or wrestler's bridge, is a bodyweight position in which a person arches the back with weight supported on the feet and the head or neck, used in wrestling and combat sports and discussed in looksmaxxing circles as a way to thicken the neck. A general reference on the bridge exercise describes it as used in sporting and self-defense settings such as wrestling, judo and mixed martial arts, and as intended mainly for lower back and gluteal strength .

name: Neck curls with plate
summary: Loaded forward neck flexion with a plate to thicken the neck; popular on forums, no appearance trials.
lead: Neck curls with a plate are a form of loaded neck flexion: a person lifts or holds a weight plate on the head while bending the neck forward, aiming to thicken the muscles at the front and sides of the neck. In looksmaxxing forums the exercise is discussed as a way to build a thicker neck and, by extension, a more masculine overall look.
claims: Neck curls produce visible progress in neck and facial appearance
Neck curls and chin tucks widen the jaw or improve the face
Starting neck curls too hard can cause soreness or other symptoms

name: Shrugs / trap training
summary: Loaded shoulder raises to build the traps and make the neck look thicker; sources cover only muscle activation, not looks.
lead: Shrugs and trapezius training are resistance exercises in which the shoulders are raised against a load, used to build the upper trapezius muscle. In looksmaxxing discussion they are mentioned as a way to make the neck look thicker by building the muscles at its base.

name: Isometric neck holds
summary: Pressing your head against your hand to thicken the neck; studied for pain and strength, never for looks.
lead: Isometric neck holds are exercises in which a person pushes the head against a resisting hand, a band or a wall without moving it, contracting the neck muscles while the head stays still. In looksmaxxing communities the approach is discussed as a way to build neck size and muscle definition, which proponents associate with a stronger-looking jaw and neck.
claims: Hands-resisted neck holds build a thicker, more masculine neck.
Stronger neck muscles improve the look of the jaw and neck line.

name: Platysmaplasty (neck band surgery)
summary: Surgery that tightens the neck's platysma muscle to remove bands and sharpen the neck line; supported by surgical case series, not trials.
lead: Platysmaplasty is a surgical procedure that modifies the platysma, the thin sheet of muscle across the front of the neck, to reduce visible vertical neck bands and improve the neck contour. It is usually performed as part of a neck lift or facelift, sometimes together with removal of submental fat .

name: Cervicoplasty / Cervical contouring
summary: Surgical contouring of neck skin, fat and muscle; documented in surgical series, with little controlled evidence.
lead: Cervicoplasty is a plastic-surgery term for contouring the neck by working on skin, fat and sometimes muscle. In aesthetic practice it is part of neck rejuvenation, and it also appears in reconstruction after burn contractures . Looksmaxxing communities group it among hardmaxxing procedures aimed at a cleaner neck and jaw transition.

name: Neck liposuction
summary: Suctioning fat from under the chin and neck; surgical case series support it, controlled trials are lacking.
lead: Neck liposuction, also called submental liposuction, removes fat beneath the chin and along the neck through small incisions using suction cannulas. It is performed to reduce a double chin and improve the neck and jawline contour, and is sometimes combined with platysma repair or other lifting techniques .
claims: Neck liposuction gives permanent results and suits people who are not 'complete jawlets'.

name: Neck fillers / skin boosters
summary: Hyaluronic acid injections for neck lines; only registered trials found, no published results reviewed.
lead: Neck fillers and skin boosters are injectable treatments, usually hyaluronic acid products, used to soften horizontal neck lines and improve neck skin quality. In looksmaxxing and aesthetic-medicine discussion they are an option for horizontal neck rhytides, sometimes called necklace lines.

name: Neck cream / retinoid for necklines
summary: Topical creams for neck lines and laxity; small product-specific studies report improvement in skin signs.
lead: Neck creams are topical cosmetic products marketed to improve lines, laxity, crepiness and pigmentation of neck and decolletage skin; some formulations contain retinoids or other active ingredients. They are a low-intensity option discussed among skincare-oriented appearance communities.

name: Tech neck correction
summary: Posture habits and exercises aimed at undoing a forward head from screen use; symptoms are studied, appearance effects are not.
lead: Tech neck, also called text neck, is an informal name for a forward-leaning head and neck posture associated with prolonged use of phones, tablets and laptops, and for the discomfort sometimes attributed to it. "Tech neck correction" refers to the exercises, ergonomic changes and posture habits that people use to reduce that posture. In looksmaxxing culture it is discussed mainly as a posture topic, because forward head carriage is said to shorten the visual neck line and soften the jaw-to-neck transition.

name: Neck stretches / chin tucks
summary: Deep neck flexor exercise used in physio for posture; forums claim it lifts the hyoid area, but no appearance studies exist.
lead: Chin tucks are a head-retraction exercise in which the chin is drawn straight back, without tilting the head down, to engage the deep neck flexors. Neck stretches and chin tucks are used in physical therapy for posture-related neck complaints and are discussed in looksmaxxing forums as a way to improve neck posture, with some users adding weighted neck curls.
claims: Chin tucks and neck curls raise the hyoid area
Adding weight to chin tucks makes visible before-and-after changes
Chin tucks correct forward head posture

name: Sternocleidomastoid (SCM) hypertrophy
summary: Building the large side-neck muscles for a thicker look; anatomy is well described, hypertrophy for appearance is unstudied.
lead: The sternocleidomastoid (SCM) is one of the largest and most superficial muscles of the neck, running on each side from the sternum and clavicle up to the mastoid process behind the ear. In looksmaxxing culture, "SCM hypertrophy" refers to building these muscles so the sides of the neck look thicker and more defined.

name: Neck-to-jaw angle (cervicomental angle) theory
summary: A profile-angle idea (about 105-120 degrees) for a clean chin-to-neck line; surgery literature describes the angle, no study supports the number.
lead: The cervicomental angle is the angle between the underside of the chin or jaw and the front of the neck, seen in profile. In aesthetic surgery literature, aging of the neck is described as including a widening of this angle along with submental fat accumulation, loss of mandibular contour and prominent platysmal bands. In looksmaxxing frameworks, a "neck-to-jaw angle theory" holds that a sharper angle in a specific range, often quoted as roughly 105 to 120 degrees, reads as more attractive.

name: Collar and shirt choice for thick neck
summary: Picking collar shapes and shirt fit to suit a thick neck; collar types are documented, effects on appearance are not studied.
lead: Collar and shirt choice for a thick neck is a clothing practice in which people select collar shapes and shirt fits to complement a larger neck, with the stated aim being to emphasize the neck. Shirt collars come in several standard shapes, including spread, point, button-down and mandarin styles.

name: Fat-loss to reveal neck
summary: Getting leaner to show neck and jaw definition; fat distribution is genetic and bone structure matters too.
lead: Fat loss to reveal the neck refers to reducing body fat so that neck and submental contours look more defined. Wikipedia notes that a double chin can arise from excess fat around the neck in some overweight people, or from a bony deficiency in people of normal weight, and that the bony form usually needs surgical correction.

name: Whey/creatine bulking for neck
summary: Using protein and creatine supplements alongside neck training to add neck size; the supplements are studied for muscle in general, not for the neck.
lead: Whey and creatine bulking for the neck refers to the practice of combining a calorie surplus, whey protein and creatine monohydrate with direct neck exercises, with the aim of increasing neck muscle size. In looksmaxxing communities a thicker neck is often discussed as contributing to a stronger-looking frame and jaw area.
claims: Supplements and a calorie surplus will thicken the neck.

name: Gua sha neck / lymphatic drainage
summary: Scraping a smooth stone along the neck and jaw, popularized on social media for debloating and a sharper jawline; clinical evidence for these aims is lacking.
lead: Gua sha is a traditional Chinese medicine practice in which a smooth tool, such as a ceramic spoon, coin or jade stone, is drawn across oiled skin. A lighter facial version applied to the jaw and neck became popular on social media in 2021 and 2022 for lymphatic drainage and skin rejuvenation.
claims: Gua sha on the neck and jaw drains lymph and sharpens the jawline.

name: Kybella for neck/jowl
summary: Deoxycholic acid injections that dissolve fat under the chin; FDA-approved for submental fat, with jowl and neck use being off-label.
lead: Kybella is a prescription injectable form of deoxycholic acid, made by Kythera Biopharmaceuticals and sold as Belkyra in some markets such as Australia. The US FDA approved it on April 29, 2015 for reducing moderate-to-severe fat below the chin, and a generic became available in April 2021.

name: Scalp micropigmentation
summary: A cosmetic tattoo of tiny pigment dots that mimics a buzzed head or denser hair; it camouflages rather than regrows hair.
lead: Scalp micropigmentation (SMP), also called a hair tattoo, is a non-surgical cosmetic tattoo that makes a bald or thinning scalp look like a close buzz cut or gives the impression of more density. It can also conceal hair transplant scars and burn or other scars on the head.
claims: SMP only suits men who keep a bald or buzzed look.
A hair transplant may be preferable to SMP if the person wants natural hair length.

name: PRP for hair
summary: Scalp injections of a person's own platelet concentrate for hair loss; small trials report gains, but the research base is limited and protocols vary.
lead: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) is a concentrate of plasma protein from a person's own blood, in which red blood cells are removed and platelets retained. Platelets are thought to release growth factors and cytokines that aid healing, though Wikipedia says its benefits remain disputed. For hair loss, PRP is injected into the scalp as an option for androgenetic alopecia and alopecia areata, sometimes discussed as an alternative or addition to minoxidil or finasteride.

name: Exosome hair therapy
summary: Scalp serums or injections of cell-derived vesicles sold as follicle revivers; only small registered trials so far.
lead: Exosome hair therapy refers to scalp treatments, applied as serums, through microneedling or by injection, that contain exosomes: nanometre-scale vesicles released by cells that carry proteins, lipids and nucleic acids. Clinics and cosmetic brands that offer it say the vesicles, usually derived from cultured mesenchymal stem cells such as umbilical cord cells, signal to dormant follicles and prompt regrowth.

name: Stem cell hair therapy
summary: Clinic injections of fat-derived or follicle-derived cells for hair regrowth; small trials registered, no approved product.
lead: Stem cell hair therapy is an umbrella term for treatments that inject or apply cells, or products derived from cells, to the scalp in order to slow hair loss or promote regrowth. Variants include adipose-derived (fat) stem cell preparations, stromal vascular fraction, cells cultured from a patient's own hair follicles, donor mesenchymal stem cells, and cell-conditioned extracts or secretomes.

name: Hair cloning
summary: Multiplying follicle cells in a lab to grow unlimited hair is a long-promised idea that remains in animal and lab research.
lead: Hair cloning, also called hair multiplication or follicle neogenesis, is a proposed regenerative approach to hair loss in which a small number of cells from healthy follicles, such as dermal papilla cells, are multiplied in the laboratory and then implanted into balding scalp to form new follicles.  It is aimed at overcoming the main limit of hair transplantation, a finite supply of donor hair.
